replaceState()

The replaceState() method performs a replace-style state update on a FeatureCell. It enters the Replace stage of the pipeline and fully replaces the current committed state with the resolved incoming value.

Unlike mergeState(), which structurally combines the existing state with an incoming value, replaceState() discards the current state and forwards the resolved incoming value as the authoritative candidate for downstream pipeline stages.

Method Contract Summary

  • Must be called after initialize()
  • Executes the full pipeline (see Full Pipeline Flow diagram)
  • Fully replaces the current committed state
  • Does not mutate existing state directly
  • Returns a Promise<void> that resolves when pipeline execution completes

replaceState() does not participate in the Merge stage and does not use any Merge behavior. The resolved incoming value becomes the candidate state directly before downstream operators, filters, reducers, and taps execute.

 Submits a replace-style state update into the pipeline. The incoming value is resolved and becomes the candidate state directly, replacing the current committed state before downstream processing occurs.

Replace operations do not use merge semantics. The incoming value becomes the authoritative state candidate after resolution.

Accepted State Input Types

The replaceState() method accepts the full range of input types defined by StateInputType<T>. These inputs determine how the Resolve stage interprets and prepares the incoming value before it replaces the current state.

Note

All accepted input types are normalized during the Resolve stage before state replacement occurs. The resolved candidate value replaces the current committed state before downstream pipeline stages execute.

Example

The replaceState() method submits a candidate value into the pipeline, where it is resolved and then replaces the current committed state before operators, filters, reducers, and taps execute.

What this does

  • Submits an incoming value for replacement
  • Discards the current committed state
  • Runs the full downstream pipeline
  • Commits the final snapshot if not suppressed

Example: Replacing Default State

{{`
@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {

  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();
  }

  replaceEmployees() {
    this.vault.replaceState([{ name: 'Alice', age: 25 }]);
  }
}

// If current state is:
// [{ name: 'John', age: 30 }]
//
// After replace:
// this.vault.state.value()
// [{ name: 'Alice', age: 25 }]
`}}
 
{{`
export const employeeCell = FeatureCell({
  key: 'employees',
  initialState: [{ name: 'John', age: 30 }]
});

employeeCell.initialize();

employeeCell.replaceState([{ name: 'Alice', age: 25 }]);

// After replace:
// employeeCell.state.value
// [{ name: 'Alice', age: 25 }]
`}}
Note

replaceState() always performs full state replacement. No merge behavior participates in this operation.
